title: Core memory unlocked #Broadway #AChorusLine #AChorusLine50 #TheatreHi...
transcript: This was maybe one of the most magical theater experiences I've ever had. And I do not say that lightly, because I never thought that I would get to see the original cast of A Chorus Line perform this material ever. And I thought it was really smart how they did it, because obviously, one. A lot of the members of the original company are sadly no longer with us. And the ones that are are not able to do the dancing that these roles require. And so, sadly, we were never going to be able to see them perform these roles full out. But what we did get was magical. From Kelly Bishop doing Sheila's monologue to Priscilla Lopez doing the entirety of nothing and Donna Mckechnie singing music in the mirror. And we also got to hear from these performers directly about their experiences working on the original production and then performing the rest of the score. We had a truly all star cast, including people like Tony Award, Jessica Voss, Krista Rodriguez. We had Jen Sarmar singing dance 10 looks three, which was everything I didn't know I needed. And of course, so many faithful recreations of these iconic dances, from the opening number to music in the mirror to the finale, all faithfully restaged by original company member by York Lee, based on the choreography of Michael Bennett. The entire evening was just such a love letter to the show and its legacy. Like, I think People today may not realize just how big a deal a Chorus Line was like this was truly the Hamilton of its day. Many credit it with single handedly saving Broadway in a very dark time. It truly redefined what musical theater could be. And to get just a small glimpse into the magic of what that original production was like 50 years ago is truly something I will never forget.
